A shared mutable byte array buffer in Properties.load could race under concurrent access. If an attacker controls the cache file, Properties.load may poison it to skip checks. Configuration serialization is not a deserialization gadget.

XmlLoader requires an explicit opt-in to load external DTDs, so it is not a P0. The resolveEntity method returns null for unmapped public IDs, which may cause the parser to fall back to systemId. XXE protection depends on whether the factory-level SAX features are actually enforced on the reader. This is a known issue.

The SAX features are correctly configured on the factory. When external DTD loading is disabled, all three features are false and validation remains true. A null public ID in resolveEntity may cause the parser to fall back to the system ID, but this is the intended secure default. If a mapped public ID points to a missing classpath resource, the resulting null stream would cause an NPE or error, yet this is not a security issue. PropertyCacheFile writes to a path specified by trusted configuration, so cache file control is expected.
